subject: C23
required_fixes: C23-R2-F1 (high): Preserve the ownership fence when recovery cannot finish. authority/import_v1_domain.rs:393-403 derives the write guard only from activity, and recover at :1543-1566 clears that activity through settle_v1 (:636-640) even when owner rollback fails and the receipt remains unsettled. Meanwhile revert at :1580-1588 promotes intended entries into written, assuming no intervening writer; cases are subsequently removed by matching ID/content alone (authority/import_v1_domain/owners.rs:1090 onward). Counterexample: interrupt at Writing before adding a case to an existing tenant with a sealed library; relaunch with its v2 Keychain unavailable so recovery retains that intended case; unlock, open the library and independently import identical case content through the ordinary C12 operation; retry rollback or relaunch. The cleared guard admits the independent write, and the old receipt can delete it. Keep affected owner scopes fenced until recovery settles, or establish durable operation provenance that cannot claim later independent work. Acceptance: exercise this failed-recovery/unlock/write/retry sequence through production interfaces; affected writes must be refused or later independent work must survive, with a truthful actionable receipt.

C23-R2-F2 (high): Enforce the import commit boundary in native admission and direct reads. tsg_matches (authority/import_v1_domain.rs:283-292) includes staged tenants in import-view matches, while waits_for_import (:1708 onward) does not cover SelectTenant. authority.rs:2880-2889 accepts any tenant in raw state, persists it as active and issues a context; snapshot.active (:1399 onward) is also unfiltered. Thus a tenant hidden from the normal list can become active before its import commits. There is a second direct-read bypass: authority/harness_history.rs:230-253 accepts OpenHarnessHistory for any valid record UUID in the current scope; the list filters staged conversations at :597 onward, but opened at :636 onward publishes their full entries without that check. A known v1 record ID can expose the staged transcript. Apply receipt eligibility at native admission and result publication, including import matches and active contexts. Acceptance: pause before commit, attempt SelectTenant using a staged ID and OpenHarnessHistory using a staged conversation ID through normal native delivery; neither authority nor content may be published until commit, and rollback must leave no active staged authority.

C23-R2-F3 (medium): Fail closed when the manifest needed to hide partial owner writes cannot be read. import_v1/receipt.rs:235-253 omits damaged/unreadable receipts and treats any receipt-directory read failure as an empty successful inventory. authority/import_v1_domain.rs:298-309 then stages and recovers only successfully decoded receipts. Interrupt after an early tenant write, damage or make its receipt unreadable, and relaunch: the saved tenant remains in destination storage but has no staging record, so it is published as ordinary committed data. A damaged-receipt count alone does not preserve DESIGN's no-partial-generation guarantee. Preserve an independently recoverable generation binding or quarantine uncertain imports when manifest inventory fails; distinguish an absent directory from an unreadable one. Acceptance: corrupt a receipt or deny receipt-directory access after an early owner write and relaunch; partial imported data/authority must remain unavailable, preexisting work must remain intact, and recovery must expose an actionable error.
evidence_gaps: C23-R2-G1: Extend the production-interface failure matrix to the three paths above. recovery.rs verifies successful startup undo before independently adding matching cases, and its sync-fault scenarios clear the fault before relaunch; these do not establish safety after recovery itself fails and normal writes resume. List-visibility assertions do not test native selection/direct history reads, and no supplied scenario combines persisted staged owner data with a damaged/unreadable receipt. Add deterministic regressions asserting ownership preservation, native context/read refusal and safe publication on relaunch. The current passing native flows and mutation guards do not establish these properties.
limitations: Independent read-only review. No application/source edits, build/test reruns, application launches, product endpoint calls or credential access. Findings follow inspected production control flow and ownership rules; they are not claimed as newly executed runtime reproductions. Only the designated verdict artifact is written.

All four supplied fingerprints independently match at the beginning and end. Verified 719 source-inventory entries, 394 direct packet references, recorded command logs/artifacts, shared dependency equivalence and exact C23 command plans. Both direct predecessors pass; 30 transitive receipt bindings match. Compared the 24 changed source inputs against attempt-01. Historical owner-accepted chunk scores are treated as history, with later phase gates checked separately.

Account-bound draft writes/rollback, conditional draft insertion/deletion and confirmed pre-write receipt journaling address substantial parts of attempt-01. The expanded tests cover every selected item's commit points across categories. A receipt serving as the logical publication manifest is a viable approach; the required fixes concern concrete gaps in its failure and native-access boundaries.

Recorded evidence passes 13 check commands, 13 test/setup commands and 3 native-preparation commands. Logs include 414 desktop frontend tests, 219 core unit tests, 18 imports_rollback tests, 8 import-module tests and targeted owner regressions. Native records pass all 8 C23 checks plus 250 C01-C22 regression checks against executable 8be1b95f41b4331bfc4e0dc026b428574a772821a2d68126a494605f0b1db99b. All 29 named C23 mutation guards report failures under mutation, four baseline targets pass three times each, and the re-anchored C12 guard is source-bound. These counts are overlapping evidence, not an independent completeness guarantee.

Native v1 data and Keychain items are synthetic fixtures. Production login-Keychain reads and real v1 profiles were not exercised; protected-profile qualification remains C25 evidence. Interruption hooks model process stops, not physical power loss. Spoken VoiceOver and signed installed-package qualification remain separate gates. No C23 workload is registered; the explicit import bounds are the applicable performance scope.
